name: James Madison
epithet: Faction, and the people as principals
dossier: Only the Federalist papers that this Gutenberg text labels MADISON are searched. The three papers labeled MADISON, with HAMILTON are in neither index.
voice: I ask how a society of different interests can govern itself.

works.title: The Federalist Papers
works.note: Project Gutenberg ebook 1404, papers this edition attributes to Madison alone

entries.claim: From the protection of different and unequal faculties of acquiring property, the possession of different degrees and kinds of property immediately results; and from the influence of these on the sentiments and views of the respective proprietors, ensues a division of the society into different interests and parties.
entries.bears: Federalist 10 traces parties to unequal faculties and to the different property those faculties acquire.

entries.claim: The House of Representatives, like that of one branch at least of all the State legislatures, is elected immediately by the great body of the people.
entries.bears: The House is said to be elected immediately by the great body of the people.

entries.claim: The federal and State governments are in fact but different agents and trustees of the people, constituted with different powers, and designed for different purposes.
entries.bears: Federal and state governments are called different agents and trustees of the people.

entries.claim: No qualification of wealth, of birth, of religious faith, or of civil profession is permitted to fetter the judgement or disappoint the inclination of the people.
entries.bears: Wealth, birth, religious faith, and civil profession are not to fetter the people's choice.

entries.claim: No law or resolution can now be passed without the concurrence, first, of a majority of the people, and then, of a majority of the States.
entries.bears: No law, he says, can pass without a majority of the people and then a majority of the states.

entries.claim: Federalist 10 derives parties from different and unequal faculties of acquiring property, and from the interests that follow.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A society of one interest is not the society he is describing.

entries.claim: The House is elected by the great body of the people, and the federal and state governments are called different agents and trustees of those people.
entries.loc: On the House and on federalism
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The people are the principals of more than one government.

entries.claim: Wealth, birth, religious faith, and profession are not qualifications for being chosen, and a law needs a majority of the people and then a majority of the states.
entries.loc: On qualifications and on the compound republic
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The people choose, and the states concur.
